article_content: James Rodriguez believes his Colombia side is fully prepared to take on host nation Brazil in the World Cup quarter-finals. On Saturday, the 22-year-old playmaker hit two goals in a 2-0 win over Uruguay, lifting his tally to five and surpassing Lionel Messi and Neymar in the tournament scoring race. His stunning volley in that match has become one of this World Cup's most memorable moments. Guided by Jose Pekerman, Colombia have enjoyed a perfect record at this World Cup, defeating Ivory Coast, Greece, and Japan, with thirteen goals scored and only two conceded. Rodriguez says they feel no pressure and are determined to keep writing history. Facing Brazil in Fortaleza, this spirited team believes their attacking flair could shake the hosts, especially as Rodriguez insists, 'We have good players and we can be dangerous.'

La sua straordinaria volée in quella partita è diventata uno dei momenti più memorabili di questo Mondiale. Sotto la guida di José Pekerman, la Colombia ha ottenuto un record perfetto in questa Coppa del Mondo, battendo Costa d'Avorio, Grecia e Giappone, con tredici gol segnati e solo due subiti. Rodriguez afferma che non sentono alcuna pressione e sono determinati a continuare a scrivere la storia. Affrontando il Brasile a Fortaleza, questa squadra vivace crede che il suo gioco offensivo possa mettere in difficoltà i padroni di casa, soprattutto perché Rodriguez insiste: 'Abbiamo buoni giocatori e possiamo essere pericolosi.'

article_content: Legendary American Football player David 'Deacon' Jones died on Monday, June 3, 2013, at the age of 74. The Hall of Fame defensive end was credited with coining the word 'sack' for his quarterback takedowns. The Washington Redskins stated that Jones died of natural causes at his home in Southern California on Monday night. Redskins general manager Bruce Allen — whose father, George, coached Jones with the Los Angeles Rams — said: 'Deacon Jones was one of the greatest players in NFL history. Off the field, he was a true giant. His passion and spirit will continue to inspire those who knew him. He was a cherished member of the Allen family, and I will always consider him my big brother.' Jones was the leader of the Rams' Fearsome Foursome from 1961 to 1971, then played for San Diego for two seasons before finishing his career with the Redskins in 1974. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1980 and made the league's 75th anniversary all-time squad. Since sacks did not become an official statistic until 1982, Jones' total remains uncertain. However, he was renowned as a premier pass rusher and team leader. He made the Pro Bowl every year from 1964 to 1970 and appeared in eight Pro Bowls overall. He was a key member of the legendary Los Angeles Rams defensive front four, known as the 'Fearsome Foursome,' with Lamar Lundy, Merlin Olsen, Rosey Grier, and Deacon Jones. He combined with fellow Hall of Famer Merlin Olsen, Rosey Grier, and Lamar Lundy on a defensive line that was often considered unblockable. George Allen, who coached the Fearsome Foursome, called Jones the 'greatest defensive end of modern football.' The Allen family had Jones present George Allen for his Hall of Fame induction in 2002. The Rams' unofficial statistics show Jones with 159.5 sacks as a Ram and 173.5 in his career. He was also one of the most durable players, missing only five games over 14 professional seasons. A 14th-round draft pick from Mississippi Valley State University in 1961, Jones was the first defensive lineman to record 100 solo tackles, achieving that milestone in 1967. His No. 75 jersey was retired by the Rams in 2009. Most recently, Jones served as the CEO of his own foundation, established in 1997. He also made several visits to active-duty troops in the Middle East.

article_content: Sabrina Moss, a 24-year-old nursery teacher and mother of one, was fatally shot outside a takeaway in Kilburn, north-west London. She had been celebrating her birthday on August 25 when a shotgun and a Mac 10 machine gun were fired. Her friend, 24-year-old Sabrina Gachette, along with two men named Mahod Ahmed and Edson Da-Silva, were also injured during the incident. Ms Gachette remains in the hospital but is recovering from her injuries. The suspect, 22-year-old Martell Warren of Willesden, north-west London, was charged with murder, multiple counts of attempted murder, and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life. Prosecutors indicate both a Mac 10 machine gun and a shotgun were used. Warren appeared via video link at the Old Bailey in Central London and was remanded in custody until a hearing on November 19. He was arrested at St Pancras International train station two days after the shooting. No comments are being accepted on the case for legal reasons.

La sua amica, la ventiquattrenne Sabrina Gachette, insieme a due uomini di nome Mahod Ahmed ed Edson Da-Silva, sono rimasti feriti durante l'incidente. La signora Gachette e' ancora ricoverata in ospedale, ma si sta riprendendo dalle ferite riportate. Il sospettato, il ventiduenne Martell Warren di Willesden, nel nord-ovest di Londra, e' stato accusato di omicidio, tentato omicidio multiplo e possesso di arma da fuoco con l'intento di mettere in pericolo la vita. Secondo i procuratori, sia una mitraglietta Mac 10 sia un fucile sono stati utilizzati. E' stato arrestato alla stazione ferroviaria di St Pancras International due giorni dopo la sparatoria. Non sono ammessi commenti sul caso per motivi legali.

article_content: Former Cleveland Police officer Wayne Scott has been found guilty of a series of serious sex crimes, including eight rapes and two serious sexual offences against a child. The 37-year-old was convicted of the rape and attempted rape of a woman after a five-day trial. Prior to this, he had already admitted raping another woman seven times over a number of years. Police are now appealing for additional victims to come forward. Detective Superintendent Peter McPhillips of Cleveland Police described Scott as a 'sexual predator' who disgraced his uniform and deserves to be behind bars. Scott was arrested in August 2011 following on-duty allegations, then suspended and ultimately dismissed. According to evidence presented at Newcastle Crown Court, Scott forcibly removed his victim's clothing before attempting to rape her, and later raped her again in his car. Scott also confessed to two common assaults, one sexual assault, and two counts of inciting a child to engage in sexual touching. He referred to himself as 'sexed up' during a police interview. Detective Superintendent McPhillips praised the determination of Scott's victims for taking the case through the courts. Scott will be sentenced on December 23 and has been remanded in custody until then.

article_content: (CNN) -- A 1-year-old child whose family disputed with a Canadian hospital over whether he should be allowed to die will likely receive an operation to insert a breathing tube by the end of the week, according to his new hospital. Joseph Maraachli, widely known as 'Baby Joseph,' is being evaluated at SSM Cardinal Glennon Children's Medical Center, a Catholic hospital in St. Louis, spokesperson Bob Davidson said. The hospital planned a press conference for Tuesday but canceled it 'because there is not yet a firm treatment plan,' Davidson noted in a statement. However, the head of pediatrics, Dr. Robert Wilmott, expects a tracheotomy to be performed by the end of the week, according to the statement. A tracheotomy is a surgical procedure creating an opening in the neck to allow breathing through a tube, offering more comfortable ventilation and enabling fluid suction. Joseph, who has a progressively worsening neurological condition, was transferred Sunday from a hospital in London, Ontario. Born in January 2010, he had been under the care of London Health Sciences Centre in Canada since October. Court documents indicate that his doctor found 'all cranial nerve functions are now absent,' leaving no hope for recovery, and recommended removing his breathing tube to allow him to die. Joseph's parents, Moe and Sana Maraachli, wanted a tracheotomy and continued mechanical ventilation so they could bring him home for family care. Joseph's aunt, Samar Nadar, explained that in 2002, the Maraachlis' daughter died at home with a tracheotomy after encountering a similar condition. In January, a Canadian Superior Court judge ruled in favor of the hospital, allowing it to remove the breathing tube without replacement and issue a do-not-resuscitate order along with palliative care recommendations. The Maraachlis sought a second opinion from a U.S. hospital. The Canadian hospital stated it would not perform the tracheotomy because it is an invasive procedure typically meant for patients requiring long-term mechanical ventilation. A statement on the Canadian hospital's website said Joseph's transfer on Sunday proceeded 'despite the strongest possible medical advice to the contrary.' Joseph's case garnered attention from pro-life organizations, including Priests for Life and the Terri Schiavo Life & Hope Network, which held prayer vigils and rallies. In February, the Canadian hospital received threats, prompting tighter security measures. Father Frank Pavone, National Director of Priests for Life, traveled to Ontario to assist with the transfer. He described the situation as 'a race against time,' stating Joseph 'needs to be in a hospital that cherishes life over the bottom line.' CNN Medical Producer Sabriya Rice contributed to this report.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Un bambino di un anno, la cui famiglia era in disputa con un ospedale canadese sulla possibilità di terminare o meno la sua vita, probabilmente riceverà un intervento per inserire un tubo respiratorio entro la fine della settimana, secondo il suo nuovo ospedale. Joseph Maraachli, conosciuto dai media come 'Baby Joseph', è in valutazione presso il SSM Cardinal Glennon Children's Medical Center, un ospedale cattolico di St. Louis, ha riferito il portavoce Bob Davidson. L’ospedale aveva programmato una conferenza stampa per martedì, ma l’ha annullata 'perché non esiste ancora un piano di trattamento definitivo', ha dichiarato Davidson in un comunicato. Tuttavia, il responsabile di pediatria, il dottor Robert Wilmott, prevede che verrà effettuata una tracheotomia entro la fine della settimana, come indicato nel comunicato. La tracheotomia è una procedura chirurgica che crea un’apertura nel collo per consentire la respirazione attraverso un tubo, offrendo una ventilazione più confortevole e facilitando l’aspirazione dei liquidi. Joseph, che soffre di un progressivo peggioramento di una condizione neurologica, è stato trasferito domenica da un ospedale di London, nell’Ontario. Nato nel gennaio 2010, era in cura presso il London Health Sciences Centre in Canada da ottobre. I documenti del tribunale mostrano che il suo medico ha riscontrato 'la totale assenza di funzioni nervose craniche', senza prospettive di miglioramento, raccomandando la rimozione del tubo respiratorio per lasciarlo morire. I genitori di Joseph, Moe e Sana Maraachli, desideravano una tracheotomia e una ventilazione meccanica continuata, così da poterlo portare a casa e prendersene cura. La zia di Joseph, Samar Nadar, ha spiegato che nel 2002 la figlia dei Maraachli è deceduta a casa con una tracheotomia dopo aver sofferto di una condizione simile. A gennaio, un giudice della Corte Superiore canadese ha deciso a favore dell’ospedale, permettendo la rimozione del tubo e l’emissione di un ordine di non rianimazione insieme a raccomandazioni per cure palliative. I Maraachli hanno cercato un secondo parere in un ospedale negli Stati Uniti. L’ospedale canadese ha affermato che non avrebbe eseguito la tracheotomia perché è una procedura invasiva, di solito destinata a chi necessita di ventilazione meccanica a lungo termine. Suo sito web ha pubblicato un comunicato in cui si afferma che il trasferimento di Joseph di domenica è avvenuto 'nonostante il più forte parere medico contrario'. Il caso di Joseph ha suscitato l’interesse di gruppi pro-life, tra cui Priests for Life e la Terri Schiavo Life & Hope Network, che hanno organizzato veglie di preghiera e manifestazioni di sostegno. A febbraio, l’ospedale canadese ha ricevuto minacce e ha rafforzato la sicurezza. Padre Frank Pavone, Direttore Nazionale di Priests for Life, si è recato in Ontario per aiutare con il trasferimento. Ha descritto la situazione come 'una corsa contro il tempo', affermando che Joseph 'ha bisogno di un ospedale che valorizzi la vita più del profitto'. La produttrice medica della CNN Sabriya Rice ha contribuito a questo servizio.

article_content: 'This terrifying moment shows a shopkeeper hitting an armed gunman with a stool and chasing him out after two warning shots were fired. Thurairagh Pirabahuran, 41, a father-of-two, grabbed the chair he had been sitting on and confronted Sheldon Green, 23, after Green pulled the trigger and demanded cash from the till. Shocked by the resistance, Green fled empty-handed.' 'Green, a known criminal who carried out a string of robberies, has been jailed for five years. Quick-thinking Mr. Pirabahuran, part-owner of Hainault Food and Wine in Ilford, Essex, said: 'I didn't want to give him the money, so I picked up the stool and hit him with it.' He was working with his business partner, Shanmuganathan Umesh, when Green burst in around 9:30 p.m. on September 17, brandishing a gun in front of a frightened female customer as the shop was about to close.' 'Despite Green firing one or two shots to show the weapon was real, Mr. Pirabahuran served the customer before she ran out. Green demanded money again, but Mr. Pirabahuran refused and used the stool to fight back. Green was later captured after stealing a phone containing a tracking device from a woman in Hackney. He tried to evade the police by jumping into a canal but soon surrendered.' 'Green admitted to nine robbery and firearms charges at London's Old Bailey. He had stolen a high-powered Yamaha motorbike, originally listed on a community forum, and used it during his crime spree. The court heard Green began targeting stores throughout East London and Essex to repay debts to a drug gang. Judge Rabinder Singh described him as a menace to the public, saying Green went on a 'crime rampage' but used no actual violence during the robberies.'

Thurairagh Pirabahuran, 41 anni, padre di due figli, ha afferrato la sedia su cui era seduto e ha affrontato Sheldon Green, 23 anni, dopo che Green aveva premuto il grilletto e richiesto denaro dalla cassa. Sconvolto dalla resistenza, Green è fuggito a mani vuote.' 'Green, un criminale noto che aveva commesso una serie di rapine, è stato condannato a cinque anni di carcere. Il rapido intervento del signor Pirabahuran, comproprietario di Hainault Food and Wine a Ilford, nell'Essex, dimostra coraggio: ‘Non volevo dargli i soldi, così ho preso lo sgabello e l'ho colpito.’ Al momento dell'irruzione, stava lavorando con il suo socio in affari, Shanmuganathan Umesh, intorno alle 21:30 del 17 settembre, mentre il negozio stava per chiudere e una cliente spaventata era presente.' 'Nonostante Green abbia sparato uno o due colpi per dimostrare che l'arma fosse reale, il signor Pirabahuran ha servito la cliente prima che scappasse. Green ha nuovamente richiesto del denaro, ma il signor Pirabahuran ha rifiutato e ha usato lo sgabello per difendersi. In seguito Green è stato catturato dopo aver rubato un telefono dotato di dispositivo di tracciamento a una donna a Hackney. Ha tentato di sfuggire alla polizia saltando in un canale, ma si è arreso poco dopo.' 'Green si è dichiarato colpevole di nove capi di accusa per rapina e reati legati alle armi da fuoco presso la Old Bailey di Londra. Aveva rubato una potente moto Yamaha, originariamente pubblicizzata su un forum di comunità, e l'ha utilizzata durante la sua serie di crimini. Il tribunale ha saputo che Green aveva iniziato a colpire negozi in tutta l'area est di Londra e nell'Essex per ripagare i suoi debiti con una gang di trafficanti. Il giudice Rabinder Singh lo ha descritto come una minaccia per il pubblico, affermando che Green aveva intrapreso una ‘furia criminale’ ma non aveva usato violenza effettiva durante le rapine.'
